books.title: The Enchanted Castle
books.author: E. Nesbit
books.why: A magic ring turns a holiday adventure into increasingly strange trouble. Funny, imaginative and occasionally eerie, with a low barrier to entry. This selection leans toward younger readers.

books.title: The Time Machine
books.author: H. G. Wells
books.why: A short, unsettling journey into humanity's distant future. Its mysteries and survival scenes provide an immediate hook, while its ideas give readers something to think about afterward.

books.title: The Hound of the Baskervilles
books.author: Arthur Conan Doyle
books.why: Sherlock Holmes, an apparently supernatural curse and a dangerous investigation on the moors. A strong standalone introduction to Holmes, with suspense that should work particularly well aloud.

books.title: The Blue Castle
books.author: L. M. Montgomery
books.why: A woman who has spent her life obeying an oppressive family decides to live on her own terms. Warm, witty and romantic, with a satisfying emotional arc and approachable prose.

books.title: The Great Gatsby
books.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald
books.why: Wealth, extravagant parties, reinvention and obsession, followed by consequences. The shortest full-length novel in the group and a different, darker emotional register. Set in the 1920s, not the present day.

books.title: The Count of Monte Cristo
books.author: Alexandre Dumas
books.translation: Anonymous English translation published by Chapman and Hall, 1846
books.why: Betrayal, imprisonment, escape, hidden wealth and an elaborate revenge. The substantial surprise selection, chosen for its momentum and intrigue. The nineteenth-century English translation is older in style than modern commercial translations.
